subject: botany_2
question_text: What is GEAC and what are its objectives?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.46, printed question 120. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: The expansion is the first mark. Get all four words: Genetic Engineering Approval Committee.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What GEAC stands for
steps.margin_note: The four words in full, then what kind of body it is.
lines: GEAC stands for the GENETIC ENGINEERING
It is the regulatory body set up by the
steps.why: Genetic modification carries the biosafety risks listed elsewhere in this chapter, so a body with the power to approve or refuse is needed.
common_mistakes: Expanding it as 'Genetic Engineering Advisory Committee'. It is APPROVAL Committee.
Saying GEAC is an international body. It is a national regulatory body.
steps.memory_tip: Approval, not advice: it can say no.

steps.label: Its objectives

lines.text: It decides whether GM research and GM releases

lines: 1. to make decisions on the VALIDITY of GM
2. to judge the SAFETY of introducing GM organisms
steps.why: Both objectives are about permission: nothing may be researched or released without GEAC's decision.
common_mistakes: Giving one objective. There are two.
Saying GEAC develops GM crops. It APPROVES or refuses them.
steps.memory_tip: Two questions it asks: is the research sound, and is the release safe.
